effects: A poll row is stored with status open and created_at set.

A created event is appended and the poll becomes the active voting target.

failures.condition: Fewer than 2 or more than 8 options are submitted.
failures.recovery: Adjust the list to at least 2 and at most 8 labels and resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected with an option-count message and nothing is stored.

failures.condition: An option label is blank or duplicates another label after trimming and case folding.
failures.recovery: Rename or remove the duplicate or blank entry, then resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected naming the offending label; no poll and no partial option set are stored.

failures.condition: The question text is blank.
failures.recovery: Enter the dinner question and resubmit.
failures.response: Creation is rejected with a question-required message.

actions.name: Create dinner poll
preconditions: The host has supplied a nonblank question and between 2 and 8 candidate place labels.
No other creation is mid-write on this device.

effects: A ballot row is stored for the poll, code, and option with cast_at and revision 1.
The tally is recomputed and returned to the voting surface.
Total ballots increases by exactly one.

failures.condition: The poll is closed.
failures.recovery: Ask the host to reopen the poll, then submit again.
failures.response: The write is rejected with response poll_closed and no ballot row is created or changed.

failures.condition: The option id is unknown or belongs to a different poll.
failures.recovery: Choose one of the options displayed for this poll.
failures.response: The write is rejected with option_not_in_poll and the tally is unchanged.

failures.condition: The voter code is empty or whitespace only.
failures.recovery: Enter a nonblank personal code and submit again.
failures.response: The write is rejected with code_required and nothing is stored.

failures.condition: A ballot already exists for this code on this poll.
failures.recovery: Use the change-vote action to move the existing ballot, or choose a different code.
failures.response: The submission is refused as duplicate_code and the existing ballot is left untouched.

actions.name: Cast a ballot
preconditions: The poll status is open.
The submitted voter code is nonblank after trimming.
The submitted option id belongs to this poll.
No ballot yet exists for this (poll id, voter code).

effects: The existing ballot's option is replaced in place and revision increments.
updated_at is refreshed while cast_at is retained.
The tally is recomputed and total ballots stays the same.

failures.condition: The poll is closed.
failures.recovery: Wait for the host to reopen the poll before changing the ballot.
failures.response: The change is rejected with response poll_closed and the ballot keeps its previous option.

failures.condition: No ballot exists for the submitted code on this poll.
failures.recovery: Use the cast-vote action to create the first ballot for that code.
failures.response: The change is rejected as no_ballot_for_code and no row is written.

failures.condition: The new option belongs to a different poll or no longer exists.
failures.recovery: Select an option shown for the current poll.
failures.response: The change is rejected with option_not_in_poll and the ballot is unchanged.

actions.name: Change own ballot
preconditions: The poll status is open.
A ballot exists for the submitted voter code on this poll.
The newly submitted option id belongs to this poll.

effects: Poll status becomes closed and closed_at is set.
A closed event is appended.
The tally becomes final and its current counts are preserved.

failures.condition: The poll is already closed.
failures.recovery: Reopen the poll first if voting must continue.
failures.response: The close is rejected as already_closed and no duplicate event is written.

failures.condition: The caller is a member rather than the host.
failures.recovery: Ask the host to perform the close.
failures.response: The close is rejected as not_host and the poll stays open.

actions.name: Close the poll
preconditions: The caller is the host for this poll.
The poll status is open.

effects: Poll status becomes open again, closed_at is cleared, and reopen_count increments.
A reopened event is appended.
All existing ballots remain untouched and the tally returns to provisional with the same counts.

failures.condition: The poll is already open.
failures.recovery: Proceed with voting; no reopen is needed.
failures.response: The reopen is rejected as already_open and nothing changes.

failures.condition: The caller is a member rather than the host.
failures.recovery: Ask the host to reopen the poll.
failures.response: The reopen is rejected as not_host and the poll stays closed.

actions.name: Reopen the poll
preconditions: The caller is the host for this poll.
The poll status is closed.

effects: Per-option counts are recomputed from stored ballots, including zero-count options.
total_ballots is reported alongside the counts and the tie set is computed from the highest count.
No code-to-choice mapping is exposed to members.

failures.condition: The poll id does not exist in the local store.
failures.recovery: Return to the setup surface or choose an existing poll.
failures.response: The read returns poll_not_found and no counts are shown.

failures.condition: The store cannot be read or parsed.
failures.recovery: Inspect the local store file, restore from the last intact state, or recreate the poll; the application must not overwrite the unreadable file silently.
failures.response: The read returns store_unreadable and the surface shows an error state without inventing counts.

actions.name: Read the aggregate
preconditions: The poll exists and its store is readable.
The caller is the host or a member of this poll.

assertions.given: A poll in open status has options A and B and no ballots.
assertions.negative: If the second submission reused ana as the code it must not add a ballot; the total would remain 1 with A=1 and B=0, never 2.
assertions.then: The tally reports A=1, B=1, total=2, and each code appears in exactly one stored ballot.
assertions.when: Member ana submits a ballot for A and member bo submits a ballot for B on the same device.

assertions.given: The poll has ballots ana to A and bo to B with total 2.
assertions.negative: If a replacement appended a second row the total would read 3 or A would still show 1; both are wrong.
assertions.then: Exactly one ana ballot remains, now on B, and the tally reads A=0, B=2, total=2.
assertions.when: Member ana re-submits with the same code ana, choosing B.

assertions.given: A poll with total 2 is in open status.
assertions.negative: A closed poll that stored the write, dropped a prior ballot, or altered the aggregate would break the freeze.
assertions.then: Each write is rejected with response poll_closed and the tally remains total 2 with identical per-option counts.
assertions.when: The host closes it and a member then submits a new ballot or changes an existing one.

assertions.given: A closed poll holds ballots A=1 and B=1, total 2.
assertions.negative: If reopening cleared ballots or added a second ballot for an existing code the total would not be 3 with those per-option counts.
assertions.then: Status is open, both prior ballots are intact, and the tally reads A=2, B=1, total=3.
assertions.when: The host reopens the poll and member cy votes for A.

assertions.given: Poll P1 has options A and B and poll P2 has options C and D.
assertions.negative: Accepting the foreign option would create a phantom row in P1 or leak P2's totals into P1.
assertions.then: The P1 submission is rejected as option_not_in_poll, P1's tally is unchanged, and P2's ballot counts only in P2.
assertions.when: A ballot for P1 is submitted using P2's option C, and separately a ballot for P2 uses D.

assertions.given: The host is on the setup surface with a nonblank question.
assertions.negative: A stored set with an empty or indistinguishable label would make later ballots and counts ambiguous.
assertions.then: Creation is rejected, the offending label is identified, and no poll or option row is stored.
assertions.when: The host submits labels that include a blank entry or two labels equal after trimming and case folding, such as Pizza and pizza.

assertions.given: The host is on the setup surface with a nonblank question.
assertions.negative: Accepting 1 option leaves nothing to choose between and accepting 9 exceeds the stated instrument size; neither may be stored.
assertions.then: The 1-option and 9-option submissions are rejected with an option-count message, while the 3-label submission creates an open poll.
assertions.when: The host submits 1 option, then 9 options, then a set of 3 distinct labels.

assertions.given: The poll is open and no ballot exists for the entered code.
assertions.negative: Accepting blank codes would collapse different members into one anonymous ballot and undercount the group.
assertions.then: The write is rejected as code_required, no ballot is stored, and the tally is unchanged.
assertions.when: A member submits a choice with an empty or whitespace-only code.

assertions.given: A poll has options and several ballots and the tally has been read once.
assertions.negative: If the store were re-initialized, partially written, or a ballot replayed on start, counts would change or double.
assertions.then: The poll reloads with the same status, the same option set, the same per-option counts and total, and no duplicated or replayed ballot.
assertions.when: The page is refreshed and the process is stopped and started again in the same application directory.

assertions.given: A poll holds an equal split such as A=2 and B=2, or any shared highest count.
assertions.negative: Naming the first or last option as winner, or hiding one tied option, misreports the group's answer.
assertions.then: Both options show the equal count and the view states that the result is a tie, listing every tied option and naming no winner.
assertions.when: The tally is displayed.

assertions.given: Any stored ballot set exists for a poll with zero-count options.
assertions.negative: A total larger than the number of distinct codes, or a tally that omits zero-count options or borrows another poll's options, is invalid.
assertions.then: The sum of per-option counts equals the number of distinct stored codes, every row corresponds to an option of this poll, and zero-count options are shown as 0.
assertions.when: The aggregate is read.

assertions.given: A closed poll holds a ballot for code ana on option A.
assertions.negative: Letting an existing voter move a vote after close would change a result the host declared final.
assertions.then: The change is rejected with poll_closed, ana's ballot keeps A, and the aggregate is unchanged.
assertions.when: Ana re-submits with the same code choosing B.

assertions.given: A poll is closed with two ballots and a member is using the console surface.
assertions.negative: If a member could reopen, or if reopening dropped ballots, control and aggregate integrity would both fail.
assertions.then: The member's attempts are rejected as not_host, while the host's reopen appends a reopened event, keeps both ballots, and returns status open.
assertions.when: The member attempts to close and then reopen the poll, after which the host reopens it.

assertions.given: Member ana has voted and opens the voting surface again.
assertions.negative: Showing other codes next to their choices would expose individual ballots that the aggregate does not require.
assertions.then: Per-option counts and the total are visible, while no other member's code is paired with a choice anywhere on the surface.
assertions.when: The tally is rendered for ana.

assertions.given: A poll holds two ballots and the host has moved it to closed status, while the shared device still shows the member voting surface.
assertions.negative: Neither a first ballot under a new code nor a replacement under an existing code may be stored while the poll is closed, and the aggregate must not shift by even one count.
assertions.then: Both writes are rejected with response poll_closed, no ballot row is added or changed, and the tally still reports the two original ballots with unchanged per-option counts.
assertions.when: A member submits a first ballot under a new code, and a different member re-submits with an existing code to change their choice.

assertions.given: An existing poll is open on the shared device and a member is at the start view.
assertions.negative: A poll created by a member, without any host declaration, would hand setup ownership to the wrong role and break the fixed option-set guarantee.
assertions.then: The attempt is refused as not_host, the setup form is not offered to the member, no poll or option row is stored, and the existing poll stays unchanged.
assertions.when: The member attempts to create a second poll through the host-only setup entry.

assertions.given: An open poll has one ballot for code ana on option A and the tally has just been displayed.
assertions.negative: If ballots lived only in memory, or if startup replayed a stored write, the count would drop to zero or double instead of staying at one.
assertions.then: The ballot is re-read with the same code and option, the per-option counts and total are identical, and no ballot is duplicated or replayed.
assertions.when: The surface is refreshed and the process is stopped and started again in the same application directory.

basis.statement: The host creates one dinner question with a fixed set of 2-8 place options before voting starts.
Members vote on the same device under a self-chosen code, one option per person, and re-submitting with the same code replaces the earlier choice so the person still holds exactly one vote.
A per-option tally is the visible deliverable, with a total that stays at 2 when two members choose different options and 2 again after one changes vote.
The host can close the poll, after which further votes return poll_closed and the stored result is unchanged, and can reopen it so a third member can vote for a total of 3.
A vote option must belong to the poll being voted on, duplicate and empty option labels and empty codes must be rejected, and votes from different polls must never merge.
Poll state and aggregate survive a page refresh and a process restart in the same directory, and a tie is displayed as a tie rather than resolved by an arbitrary winner.
The upstream product is a Nextcloud server application in PHP and JS/Vue, positioned as a free meeting-schedule tool similar to Doodle rather than a standalone same-device poll page.
The poll entity declares only datePoll and textPoll types plus a simple voting variant, oriented to date or text option scheduling rather than a generic single-choice question.
A vote is stored per option as yes, no, or maybe, and the poll carries allowMaybe, useNo, and result-visibility settings that govern those answer modes.

Vote rows are soft-deleted records carrying poll id, user id, option id, an option text snapshot, an option hash, and an answer, so a vote is bound to a poll and an option record rather than to free text.
Option identity in the vote is cryptographically derived from the poll id plus the option text, and a separate accessor exposes the stored hash so text and hash mismatches can be detected.

Poll lifecycle is driven by an integer expiry timestamp: a poll is expired when expire is greater than zero and less than now, and voting is denied while expired; no explicit open or closed boolean or reopen field appears.
Archival is separate from closing: a deleted timestamp marks the poll archived, and the status payload distinguishes archived from expired.
Result visibility is a three-way setting of always, closed, or never; editors always see results, participants see them per the setting, and the legacy value expired is mapped to closed.
Participation identity is a Nextcloud user identity: polls store an owner id, votes store a user id, and voting is restricted to external, user, or admin user types.
Anonymity is a poll setting with a lockable state: a negative anonymous value means real anonymous and cannot be changed back.

Access is private or open, roles include owner, admin, user, email, contact, external, and none, and more than twenty named permissions cover edit, vote, results, usernames, options, comments, sharing, download, deanonymization, and changing foreign votes.
Changing another participant's votes and deanonymizing are separately gated privileges tied to edit rights, an unrestricted poll owner, and an unlocked anonymity setting.
Participant option creation is a proposal mode of disallow, allow, or review with an optional proposal expiry, and public shares are barred from adding options.
Vote volume controls exist as maxVotesPerUser and maxVotesPerOption, limits on votes rather than on the number of poll options.
Cloning produces a private, deanonymized copy titled Clone of ... with settings carried over and no votes, and deletion supports an auto-delete offset in days.

Documented capabilities include hiding results, obfuscating names, automatic expiry, participant-added options, per-option and per-user vote limits, invitations, spreadsheet or HTML export, reminders, comments, confirming options after closing, notifications, calendar conflict hints, and a REST API.

The README states the app is not maintained by Nextcloud despite living in the Nextcloud GitHub organisation, and its screenshots describe managing and creating polls, many configuration options, sharing a poll, and voting on mobile.
Licensing is GNU AGPL version 3 in COPYING with AGPL-3.0-or-later SPDX headers in the PHP files, recorded as fixed_notice_located_spdx_not_independently_verified.
Upstream was not executed: the snapshot records upstream_status not_run, so all upstream statements are static readings of four pinned files rather than observed behavior.
The supplied upstream inventory is only COPYING, README.md, lib/Db/Poll.php, and lib/Db/Vote.php; routing, controllers, services, mappers, migrations, and frontend are absent.

Model closing and reopening as explicit host-owned poll status transitions with recorded events, instead of reusing an expiry timestamp as the only way to stop voting, so a closed poll rejects writes with poll_closed and a reopened poll accepts new voters.
Represent a ballot as poll id plus pseudonym code plus one option id with uniqueness on poll id and code, so re-voting replaces the ballot and the aggregate is recomputed from ballots.
Give options stable poll-scoped ids, validate that a ballot's option belongs to the same poll, and reject duplicate or empty option labels at creation.
Use one durable local store in the application directory with atomic writes and derive totals from stored ballots on load, so refresh and same-directory restart reproduce identical state.
Display ties as equal counts with every tied option listed, no winner designation, and no synthesized tiebreaker.
Separate a host setup and control surface from a member voting and result surface, both usable sequentially on one device without per-member accounts.

Borrow upstream configurability only where it maps to this scenario, such as result visibility and one-vote-per-person enforcement, and leave out accounts, shares, groups, REST API, reminders, comments, calendar integration, anonymity machinery, and option proposals.

How the upstream aggregate is computed and displayed, including counts, percentages, charts, total participants, and tie presentation, cannot be determined because no tally, mapper, controller, or frontend file is in the supplied inventory.
Upstream reopen-after-close behavior is unknown; the supplied entity exposes only expire and deleted, and no reopen action was read.
Whether upstream supports same-device sequential voting under self-declared pseudonyms without accounts is unknown and is contradicted by the user-type gate on voting.
Upstream rejection of duplicate option labels, empty option labels, or empty participant identifiers is not evidenced in the supplied files.
No upstream rule limiting a poll to 2-8 options was found; the discovered limits apply to votes per user and votes per option.
Runtime behavior, persistence across restarts, and any error code such as poll_closed were neither executed nor observed upstream because upstream_status is not_run.

product_shape.audience: A small group standing around one shared device deciding where to eat, plus one host who sets up and controls the poll; no accounts, invitations, or remote participants.
product_shape.boundary: One directory hosts one or more polls. Each poll is a question with a fixed set of 2-8 predefined place options, identified by a poll id that scopes its options, ballots, and aggregate. Members identify themselves only by a self-chosen pseudonym code at the moment of voting, hold exactly one ballot per poll, and may replace that ballot by re-submitting the same code. The host creates the poll, controls a single open/closed transition (with reopen), and reads the same aggregate as members. The tally is always computed from stored ballots, survives refresh and a same-directory process restart, and reports ties as ties.
product_shape.delivery_profile: Single-device browser application served from one application directory with a local durable store; host and member surfaces are used sequentially on the same screen; no server accounts, network distribution, or background services.

product_shape.name: Same-Device Dinner Poll
product_shape.value: The group gets one trustworthy per-option tally of a single dinner question, with one ballot per self-chosen code, a frozen result while closed, and a preserved aggregate across refresh and process restart.

roles.data_scope: All poll configuration, the option set, aggregate counts and totals, poll status, and the close/reopen event log; no listing that maps other members' codes to their choices.
roles.goal: Pose one dinner question with a fixed option set, keep the poll open while the group votes, close it to freeze the result, and reopen it only when the group needs to continue.

roles.goal: Express one place preference under a personal code, change that preference without gaining a second vote, and read the current aggregate.
roles.name: Member

rules.statement: A poll carries exactly one question and between 2 and 8 predefined options; a creation with fewer than 2 or more than 8 options fails and stores nothing.
Each option has a stable id scoped to its poll; labels are trimmed and case-folded for duplicate detection, and blank or duplicate labels are rejected before anything is stored.
A ballot is uniquely identified by poll id plus voter code; the code must be nonblank, and submitting again with the same code replaces that ballot instead of adding a second one.
A ballot's option must belong to the same poll as the ballot; an unknown option or an option from another poll is rejected and never recorded.
All reads and writes are scoped by poll id, so options, ballots, and counts from different polls never mix and a foreign option cannot enter another poll's aggregate.
While a poll is closed, every ballot write, new or changed, is rejected with response poll_closed and the stored ballots and aggregate remain unchanged.
Reopening sets the poll back to open, appends a reopened event, keeps every existing ballot, and admits new codes and replacements under the same open-poll rules.

The aggregate is recomputed from stored ballots on every read: one count per option including zeros, a total equal to the number of distinct codes, and all options sharing the highest count reported as tied with no winner field.

Poll state, options, ballots, and lifecycle events live in one local store inside the application directory, written atomically and reloaded at start, so refresh and same-directory process restart reproduce the same status and aggregate.
Only the host may create a poll, close it, and reopen it; members may only cast or change their own ballot under their code and read the aggregate.
A member's code is used only to locate their own ballot; the aggregate surfaces no code-to-choice mapping, so no member can read another member's individual choice.

scope_options.name: Core single-choice poll on one device
scope_options.rationale: The minimum recognizable product: one question, 2-8 fixed options, one ballot per nonblank code, replacement by the same code, and a derived per-option tally read on the same screen.

scope_options.name: Explicit host close and reopen
scope_options.rationale: The scenario requires a manual freeze and a later reopen with preserved ballots, which the upstream expiry timestamp cannot express; this slice adds the two host transitions and their events.

scope_options.name: Durable local store across restart
scope_options.rationale: Acceptance requires identical state after refresh and a same-directory process restart; this slice supplies one atomic file-backed store and load-time recomputation instead of in-memory state.

scope_options.name: Several polls coexisting in one directory
scope_options.rationale: The acceptance rule that different polls never mix implies more than one poll can exist; this slice adds poll selection or ids while keeping every option, ballot, and count scoped to its poll.

scope_options.name: Optional result visibility setting
scope_options.rationale: Maps upstream's always/closed/never result visibility onto this product as an optional host setting; without it members see the live tally, which is the scenario default.

scope_options.name: Voter code confirmation to reduce collisions
scope_options.rationale: Because a code is the ballot key, two members choosing the same code would overwrite each other; an optional confirmation or code-list check makes that collision visible without changing the one-ballot rule.

findings.statement: The host creates one dinner question with a fixed set of 2–8 place options before voting starts.
Members vote on the same device under a self-chosen code (pseudonym), one option per person; re-submitting with the same code replaces the earlier choice so a person still holds exactly one vote.
A per-option tally is the visible deliverable: two people on different options must show total 2 with 1/1, and after one changes vote still total 2 (0/2).
The host can close the poll; after closing, further votes return poll_closed and the stored result is unchanged. The host can reopen, after which a third member can vote for a total of 3.
A vote option must belong to the poll being voted on; duplicate options and an empty code must be rejected, and votes from different polls must never be merged.
Poll state and aggregate must survive a page refresh and a process restart in the same directory, and a tie must be displayed as a tie rather than resolved by an arbitrary winner.
The upstream product is a Nextcloud server application written in PHP and JS/Vue, positioned as a free meeting-schedule tool similar to Doodle, not a standalone same-device poll page.

The poll entity has exactly two declared poll types, datePoll and textPoll, plus a 'simple' voting variant; the model is oriented to date/text option scheduling rather than a generic single-choice question.
A vote is stored per option as an answer of yes, no, or maybe, not as a single selected option; the poll carries allowMaybe and useNo settings that govern those answer modes.

Votes are soft-deleted rows carrying pollId, userId, option id, a snapshot of the option text, an option hash, and the answer, so a vote row is bound to a poll and an option record rather than to a free-text answer.

Option identity in the vote is cryptographically derived from the poll id plus the option text, and a separate accessor exposes the raw stored hash so mismatches between text and hash can be detected.

Poll lifecycle is driven by an integer expiry timestamp: a poll is expired when expire > 0 and expire < now, and voting is denied whenever the poll is expired. No explicit open/closed boolean or reopen field appears in the supplied Poll entity.
Archival is separate from closing: a deleted timestamp marks the poll archived, and the entity distinguishes isArchived from isExpired in its status payload.
Result visibility is a three-way poll setting (always, closed, never); editors always see results, participants see them only per the setting, and the legacy value 'expired' is mapped to 'closed'.

Participation identity is a Nextcloud user identity: the poll stores an owner user id, each vote stores a userId, and voting is restricted to external, user, or admin user types (other external types must register first).
Anonymity is a poll setting with a lockable state: a negative anonymous value means real anonymous and is treated as locked so the setting cannot be changed back.

Access and roles are granular: access is private or open, roles include owner/admin/user/email/contact/external/none, and there are more than twenty named permissions covering edit, vote, see results, see usernames, add options, comment, share, download, deanonymize, and change foreign votes.
Changing another participant's votes and deanonymizing are separately gated privileges tied to edit rights, an unrestricted poll owner, and an unlocked anonymity setting.
Option creation by participants is a configurable proposal mode (disallow, allow, review) with an optional proposal expiry, and public shares are explicitly barred from adding options.
Vote volume controls exist as maxVotesPerUser and maxVotesPerOption, i.e. limits on votes, not a limit on the number of poll options.
Cloning a poll produces a private, deanonymized copy titled 'Clone of …' with settings carried over and no votes; deletion/archive supports an auto-delete offset in days.

Documented product-level capabilities include hiding results, obfuscating participant names, automatic expiry, participant-added options, per-option/per-user vote limits, invitations, export to spreadsheet/HTML, reminders, comments, confirming options after closing, notifications, calendar conflict hints, and a REST API.

The README states the app is not maintained by Nextcloud despite living in the Nextcloud GitHub organisation, and its screenshots describe managing/creating polls, many configuration options, sharing a poll, and voting on mobile.

findings.rationale: Upstream couples stoppage to expire and has no reopen field in the supplied entity; the scenario requires manual close and explicit reopen.
findings.statement: Model closing/reopening as an explicit poll status transition owned by the host, instead of reusing an expiry timestamp as the only way to stop voting; store close and reopen events so a closed poll rejects writes with poll_closed and a reopened poll accepts new voters.

findings.rationale: Upstream's per-option yes/no/maybe rows with user ids do not satisfy one-person-one-choice on a shared device.
findings.statement: Represent a ballot as (poll id, pseudonym code, single option id) with uniqueness on (poll id, code); a re-vote by the same code replaces that ballot rather than appending a second one, and the aggregate is recomputed from ballots.

findings.rationale: Binds the scenario's option-membership and duplicate/empty rejection rules to identity rather than free text.
findings.statement: Give options stable poll-scoped ids and validate that a submitted option id belongs to the submitted poll; normalize labels and reject duplicates and empty option labels at creation.

findings.rationale: Scenario requires same-directory process restart persistence; no server database or account layer is in scope.
findings.statement: Use a single durable local store in the application directory with atomic writes, and derive totals from stored ballots on load so refresh and restart reproduce identical state.

findings.rationale: Explicit acceptance rule; differs from any winner-oriented framing.
findings.statement: Display ties as equal counts with all tied options listed and no winner designation, and never synthesize a tiebreaker.

findings.rationale: product_shape_guidance calls for pseudonyms and host/member actions with no remote authentication platform.
findings.statement: Separate host surface (create poll, set options, close, reopen, view tally) from participant surface (enter code, select one option, submit, see current tally), both usable sequentially on one device without per-member accounts.

findings.rationale: Keeps the product inside the leaf's defining core and out of scheduling/survey territory.
findings.statement: Borrow upstream's configurability ideas only where they map to this scenario (result visibility during/after voting, one-vote-per-person enforcement); do not import Nextcloud accounts, shares, groups, REST API, reminders, comments, or calendar integration.
How the upstream aggregate is computed and displayed (counts, percentages, chart, tie presentation) cannot be determined: no tally, mapper, controller, or frontend file is in the supplied inventory.
Upstream reopen-after-close behavior is unknown; the supplied entity exposes only expire and deleted, and no reopen action was read.

Whether upstream supports same-device sequential voting under self-declared pseudonyms without accounts is unknown and is contradicted by the user-type gate on voting; no such path appears in the supplied files.
Upstream rejection of duplicate option labels, empty option labels, or empty participant identifiers is not evidenced in the supplied files.
No upstream rule limiting a poll to 2–8 options was found; the discovered limits apply to votes per user and votes per option.
Runtime behavior, persistence across restarts, and any error code such as poll_closed were not executed or observed upstream (upstream_status not_run).

The supplied upstream inventory is four files only (COPYING, README.md, lib/Db/Poll.php, lib/Db/Vote.php); entity definitions are visible but routing, controllers, services, mappers, migrations, and frontend are absent.

gaps.statement: Upstream status is not_run and no execution was permitted: all upstream findings are static readings of four pinned files, so no observed runtime behavior exists for either product.

No aggregation/tally implementation was supplied (no mapper, service, controller, or frontend), so the upstream per-option counts, percentages, chart behavior, and total-participant display remain unknown.
Upstream close and reopen semantics cannot be established from Poll.php and Vote.php: stopping votes depends on the expire timestamp, and no reopen operation or explicit closed flag was read.

No upstream evidence supports same-device sequential pseudonymous voting; the voting gate requires an external, user, or admin identity. Whether any accountless public-share path exists is outside the supplied files.
Upstream validation for duplicate option labels, empty option text, empty voter identifiers, and option-to-poll membership at write time is not present in the supplied entity files.
No upstream 2–8 option-count constraint was found; only vote limits per user and per option are evidenced. The scenario's option ceiling is a product requirement, not an upstream observation.
Tie handling upstream is unknown; no comparison or ranking logic was supplied, and the results view is not present.
Effect of editing option text after votes exist is unknown: the vote stores both option text and a text-derived hash, and a raw-hash accessor exists, but the reconciling code was not supplied.
Durability across refresh or process restart was neither tested nor evidenced for either product; persistence behavior for the scenario remains a design requirement rather than an observation.

License status is fixed_notice_located_spdx_not_independently_verified; COPYING matches AGPL-3.0 text and file headers declare AGPL-3.0-or-later, but no independent SPDX verification or runtime packaging check was performed.

basis.statement: The host creates one dinner question with a fixed set of 2-8 place options before voting starts.
Members vote on the same device under a self-chosen code, one option per person, and re-submitting with the same code replaces the earlier choice so the person still holds exactly one vote.
A per-option tally is the visible deliverable, with a total that stays at 2 when two members choose different options and 2 again after one changes vote.
The host can close the poll, after which further votes return poll_closed and the stored result is unchanged, and can reopen it so a third member can vote for a total of 3.
A vote option must belong to the poll being voted on, duplicate and empty option labels and empty codes must be rejected, and votes from different polls must never merge.
Poll state and aggregate survive a page refresh and a process restart in the same directory, and a tie is displayed as a tie rather than resolved by an arbitrary winner.
The upstream product is a Nextcloud server application in PHP and JS/Vue, positioned as a free meeting-schedule tool similar to Doodle rather than a standalone same-device poll page.
The poll entity declares only datePoll and textPoll types plus a simple voting variant, oriented to date or text option scheduling rather than a generic single-choice question.
A vote is stored per option as yes, no, or maybe, and the poll carries allowMaybe, useNo, and result-visibility settings that govern those answer modes.

Vote rows are soft-deleted records carrying poll id, user id, option id, an option text snapshot, an option hash, and an answer, so a vote is bound to a poll and an option record rather than to free text.
Option identity in the vote is cryptographically derived from the poll id plus the option text, and a separate accessor exposes the stored hash so text and hash mismatches can be detected.

Poll lifecycle is driven by an integer expiry timestamp: a poll is expired when expire is greater than zero and less than now, and voting is denied while expired; no explicit open or closed boolean or reopen field appears.
Archival is separate from closing: a deleted timestamp marks the poll archived, and the status payload distinguishes archived from expired.
Result visibility is a three-way setting of always, closed, or never; editors always see results, participants see them per the setting, and the legacy value expired is mapped to closed.
Participation identity is a Nextcloud user identity: polls store an owner id, votes store a user id, and voting is restricted to external, user, or admin user types.
Anonymity is a poll setting with a lockable state: a negative anonymous value means real anonymous and cannot be changed back.

Access is private or open, roles include owner, admin, user, email, contact, external, and none, and more than twenty named permissions cover edit, vote, results, usernames, options, comments, sharing, download, deanonymization, and changing foreign votes.
Changing another participant's votes and deanonymizing are separately gated privileges tied to edit rights, an unrestricted poll owner, and an unlocked anonymity setting.
Participant option creation is a proposal mode of disallow, allow, or review with an optional proposal expiry, and public shares are barred from adding options.
Vote volume controls exist as maxVotesPerUser and maxVotesPerOption, limits on votes rather than on the number of poll options.
Cloning produces a private, deanonymized copy titled Clone of ... with settings carried over and no votes, and deletion supports an auto-delete offset in days.

Documented capabilities include hiding results, obfuscating names, automatic expiry, participant-added options, per-option and per-user vote limits, invitations, spreadsheet or HTML export, reminders, comments, confirming options after closing, notifications, calendar conflict hints, and a REST API.

The README states the app is not maintained by Nextcloud despite living in the Nextcloud GitHub organisation, and its screenshots describe managing and creating polls, many configuration options, sharing a poll, and voting on mobile.
Licensing is GNU AGPL version 3 in COPYING with AGPL-3.0-or-later SPDX headers in the PHP files, recorded as fixed_notice_located_spdx_not_independently_verified.
Upstream was not executed: the snapshot records upstream_status not_run, so all upstream statements are static readings of four pinned files rather than observed behavior.
The supplied upstream inventory is only COPYING, README.md, lib/Db/Poll.php, and lib/Db/Vote.php; routing, controllers, services, mappers, migrations, and frontend are absent.

Model closing and reopening as explicit host-owned poll status transitions with recorded events, instead of reusing an expiry timestamp as the only way to stop voting, so a closed poll rejects writes with poll_closed and a reopened poll accepts new voters.
Represent a ballot as poll id plus pseudonym code plus one option id with uniqueness on poll id and code, so re-voting replaces the ballot and the aggregate is recomputed from ballots.
Give options stable poll-scoped ids, validate that a ballot's option belongs to the same poll, and reject duplicate or empty option labels at creation.
Use one durable local store in the application directory with atomic writes and derive totals from stored ballots on load, so refresh and same-directory restart reproduce identical state.
Display ties as equal counts with every tied option listed, no winner designation, and no synthesized tiebreaker.
Separate a host setup and control surface from a member voting and result surface, both usable sequentially on one device without per-member accounts.

Borrow upstream configurability only where it maps to this scenario, such as result visibility and one-vote-per-person enforcement, and leave out accounts, shares, groups, REST API, reminders, comments, calendar integration, anonymity machinery, and option proposals.

How the upstream aggregate is computed and displayed, including counts, percentages, charts, total participants, and tie presentation, cannot be determined because no tally, mapper, controller, or frontend file is in the supplied inventory.
Upstream reopen-after-close behavior is unknown; the supplied entity exposes only expire and deleted, and no reopen action was read.
Whether upstream supports same-device sequential voting under self-declared pseudonyms without accounts is unknown and is contradicted by the user-type gate on voting.
Upstream rejection of duplicate option labels, empty option labels, or empty participant identifiers is not evidenced in the supplied files.
No upstream rule limiting a poll to 2-8 options was found; the discovered limits apply to votes per user and votes per option.
Runtime behavior, persistence across restarts, and any error code such as poll_closed were neither executed nor observed upstream because upstream_status is not_run.

rules.statement: A poll carries exactly one question and between 2 and 8 predefined options; a creation with fewer than 2 or more than 8 options fails and stores nothing.
Each option has a stable id scoped to its poll; labels are trimmed and case-folded for duplicate detection, and blank or duplicate labels are rejected before anything is stored.
A ballot is uniquely identified by poll id plus voter code; the code must be nonblank, and submitting again with the same code replaces that ballot instead of adding a second one.
A ballot's option must belong to the same poll as the ballot; an unknown option or an option from another poll is rejected and never recorded.
All reads and writes are scoped by poll id, so options, ballots, and counts from different polls never mix and a foreign option cannot enter another poll's aggregate.
While a poll is closed, every ballot write, new or changed, is rejected with response poll_closed and the stored ballots and aggregate remain unchanged.
Reopening sets the poll back to open, appends a reopened event, keeps every existing ballot, and admits new codes and replacements under the same open-poll rules.

The aggregate is recomputed from stored ballots on every read: one count per option including zeros, a total equal to the number of distinct codes, and all options sharing the highest count reported as tied with no winner field.

Poll state, options, ballots, and lifecycle events live in one local store inside the application directory, written atomically and reloaded at start, so refresh and same-directory process restart reproduce the same status and aggregate.
Only the host may create a poll, close it, and reopen it; members may only cast or change their own ballot under their code and read the aggregate.
A member's code is used only to locate their own ballot; the aggregate surfaces no code-to-choice mapping, so no member can read another member's individual choice.

schema_contract:
Exact root keys: schema, product_shape, roles, objects, actions, surfaces,
journeys, rules, assertions, scope_options, basis, gaps; schema is atlas.product-reference.v1.
product_shape={name,audience,value,delivery_profile,boundary,excluded}. roles rows
{id,name,goal,data_scope}; objects {id,name,fields:[{name,meaning}],states,relations:[{object_id,meaning}]};
actions {id,name,role_ids,object_ids,surface_ids,rule_ids,preconditions,effects,
failures:[{condition,response,recovery}],transitions:[{object_id,from_states,to_state}],basis_ids,depends_on};
surfaces {id,name,kind,purpose,role_ids,action_ids,sections,navigation,states:{loading,empty,no_results,error,forbidden},
query:{search,filter,sort,pagination,bulk,export}}; journeys {id,name,goal,role_ids,
steps:[{surface_id,action_id,role_id,success}],completion,recovery}; rules
{id,statement,object_ids,basis_ids}; assertions {id,given,when,then,negative,action_ids,rule_ids,journey_ids};
scope_options {id,name,journey_ids,extra_action_ids,depends_on,rationale}; basis
{id,kind,statement,source_ids,depends_on}, kind in requirement/upstream_observation/
design_inference/unknown; gaps {id,statement,core,action_ids,resolution}. IDs are
lowercase letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. Every action is asserted and has an
entry surface/object; every surface/action relation is symmetric. Only fixed trusted
IDs may appear in basis source_ids. Unknown core gaps block a complete reference.
Types: every scalar name/goal/meaning/statement/condition/response/recovery and
assertion given/when/then/negative is a NONBLANK STRING (negative describes the
negative expectation; it is not a boolean). product_shape audience/value/
delivery_profile/boundary are strings. surfaces states and query values are
nonblank explanatory strings, including an explicit reason when not applicable.
All *_ids, depends_on, sections, navigation, preconditions, effects, excluded,
from_states, object states, and source_ids are lists of strings. surface.states
and surface.query are exact-key maps of explanatory strings. gaps.core is the only boolean in the
reference schema. All IDs are globally unique across collections. Action failures,
preconditions and effects must be nonempty. A design_inference basis must depend_on
at least one known basis ID. Scope options select entire journeys plus dependency
closure, and need assertions whose action_ids and journey_ids are entirely within
that option; these assertions must cover all selected actions, rules and journeys.
Do not attach every unrelated journey to one assertion: reference the specific
journeys that the given/when/then actually tests. This is schema guidance, not an
instruction to limit product capability or weaken the confirmed scenario.
For UI products, separate preparation/input actions from submit/commit actions
when they have different effects or recovery. Model entry and navigation as
surfaces where appropriate. Keep assertions independently testable and avoid
duplicating unrelated journeys in one assertion or scope slice.
Enums are exact: surfaces.kind is web/desktop/cli/api/library/other; basis.kind is
requirement/upstream_observation/design_inference/unknown. Every object relation
must name an existing object. Every action has nonempty role_ids, object_ids,
surface_ids, basis_ids, preconditions, effects, and failures; action surface links
are symmetric and each action has an assertion. Transitions must name an action
object and states declared by that object. Every surface action link is symmetric,
all navigation IDs name surfaces, and at least one role can use each action surface.
Journey steps must agree with the journey, action, and surface role sets. Every
assertion rule must be used by one asserted action; every rule has an assertion.
Basis dependencies and action/scope dependencies are acyclic. Upstream basis
source_ids must be trusted and must have host-pinned observation evidence. Core
gaps block completion. Diagnostics are additive: fix each reported issue while
preserving all confirmed business behavior and all other valid graph content.
